rationale.campaign_length: 20 shared missions plus 2 exclusive missions, with the option to continue as B59.
rationale.colonization: There is no colonial main line.
rationale.complexity: Fort defense, relations, and the shared alliance mechanics all require attention.
rationale.dark_story: It has a background of war and refugees; the route focuses on shelter and protection.
rationale.difficulty: It has a defensive foundation, but expansion and diplomacy still require patience.
rationale.diplomacy: Religious diplomats, neighboring relations, and Luna Sway are important.
rationale.early_pressure: A one-province Free City must keep stronger princes from moving in.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Urban workshops appear in the idea background, but spellcasting is not the core.
rationale.narrative_density: The fortress history, neutrality, and aid to refugees form a distinctive story.
rationale.tall_play: The exclusive missions build the capital defenses.
rationale.trade_economy: It has the shared urban-economy line, but leans toward fort defense.
rationale.warfare: The focus is holding the city and defense, although alliances may still lead to war.

identity.appearance: A republican Free City in 1444; one of four Luna River countries grouped in the scoring table.

successors.relationship: Can be formed after the shared finale and decision; this changes the Tag and mission tree.

description.text: The most unique and storied structure of Bellacaire is the looming fortress of Bellac's Rock, first built by the King of Verne, Bellac Vernid, in 587 AA as a border fortress against Dameria. For centuries it stood against the ambitions of the north, up until it was seized from the Vernids in 917 AA, acting as a bastion against her original owners until it came under siege and occupation during the War of the Sorcerer-King. Despite its long and tumultuous history, Bellac's Rock is as sturdy as ever, a mighty citadel that continues to guard the lands around it.

description.text: When the winds of war blew across the Upper Luna, Bellacaire organized a neutrality pact with her fellow Free Cities of the river. Though it was ultimately short lived, the brief moment of unity along the Luna is a goal every Bellacairey hopes to replicate, to forge a realm strong enough to protect itself from being pulled into the conflicts of others.

description.text: Despite our city's declared neutrality in the Lilac Wars, in the final days of the conflict she became the site of a brutal, yet inspiring, battle. The treacherous Cestiranders, recently supporters of the Rose Party, charged towards the city while the Galéinni did the same, both powers seeking to seize Bellacaire for their own ambitions. They met outside our gates, clashing in bloody melee while our own warriors took the field to defend the city. After four days and three nights, the invading forces were both forced to withdraw, for the guard of Bellacaire had ensured she would continue to stand free.

description.text: Running along the Luna River, the Lunawalk is where most Damerians settled after the fall of Bellac's Rock, establishing a patrician district along the gentle and serene banks. Far from reach of the great shadow cast by the Rock and gently lit by the moon at night, it is the most prestigious neighborhood in the city.
description.text_en: Running along the Luna River, the Lunawalk is where most Damerians settled after the fall of Bellac's Rock, establishing a patrician district along the gentle and serene banks. Far from reach of the great shadow cast by the Rock and gently lit by the moon at night, it is the most prestigious neighborhood in the city.

description.text: On the other side of the city, far from the opulent abodes of the Lunawalk, the workshops and laboratories of the Drabsburd buzz and churn night and day. The strange gadgets and trinkets produced by the gnomes of the district are awe-inspiring to the populace, and the city government largely leaves the gnomes to innovate and invent at will, so long as they enforce safe practices and procedures.

description.text: In the end, it truly doesn't matter who rests upon the throne of the Regent Court, for all of us shall know for sure when we pass from this world. Here one can find Adeanics and Corinites living in peace, free from the dogmatic hatred that drives their religious compatriots to battle outside the city.

description.text: The horrors of the war between the Corinite and Adeanic Leagues has left countless refugees and orphans in its wake, and the majority of the Empire is content to let them suffer in silence. This will not stand for us. The Pink Stripe is an organization based in Bellacaire to assist and nurture those devastated by war and disaster, regardless of creed, allegiance, race, or otherwise. Already they've established charters across Anbennar, looking after those that have been left behind.

description.text:
“The greatest rulers preside not over a mere reign but an Era, a period which eclipses those ahead and behind in its profundity and prolificity. They understand that the legacy of the patron is his clients.”
Tomás of Vallusna, ‘The Statesman’

description.text:
“The imitation of style necessitates the imitation of form, and therefore of function. When we build a colonnade inspired by the formal markets of Old Dameria, we are inspired also by the conversation held along that colonnade, the type of life enabled by the structure we seek to recreate. The rhetorical tradition, the vibrant public life, even the raucous protest – all are made possible by the decision, made once again, to build space for them.”
Saman of Fowlbarn, ‘The Life Of Stone’

description.text:
“Even in those realms which had not subordinated their government to an association of guild-backed aldermen, the Guild had been the fundamental unit of urban life in the Eastern Dameshead long before Pashainé’s emergence as a coherent state.

This had three major consequences. First, the codification of a sort of corporate democracy, a belief that society was best forged under a competing set of mutually-exerted pressures, by groups representing collectives of the population - even if these were subject to a monarch or a so-called ’Executive Guild’. Second, an emphasis on economic prosperity, the brass tacks ‘shopkeeper diplomacy’ for which Pashainé became notorious. Third, a relentless focus on urbanisation and the vertical integration of industry.”
Silvard Dove, ‘An Economic History of Cannor’

description.text:
“The poet Milian said that the Pashainéy is uniquely noble, having inherited the bravery of his Vernman father and the dignity of his Damerian mother. As a second daughter, I seem to have been left with the libido and stubbornness.”
Genaia ‘Geni’ Cadesna sina Bellacaire, ‘Memoirs Of A Fallen Countess’

description.text:
“Consider the conflict between Corinism and the Court which had so split the Valley. Consider, then, an unusually literate and engaged populace with a political impetus to see theological ruptures healed. Consider finally the Ravelian Lodge, which in its structure mimics the voluntary association basis of the guild. No population on Halann was more ready to embrace not merely the articles of belief but the basic organisational structure of Ravelianism.”
Leande Bellac, ‘Apologetics’

description.text:
“Over the course of the eighteenth century, the slowly aggregating impact of the Verdancy became more and more clear across the entire Luna watershed. Land which had once been among the most fertile in Cannor gave harvest perhaps once in two years, while the concomitant soil pollution devastated the Valley’s few remaining natural forests. The result was an exodus of the population from the countryside and an even greater urbanisation of Pashainé, inadvertently birthing a contentious café and street culture; this would dominate the labour politics of the following hundred years, erupting again and again into civil unrest. You will find few along the Valley who have much to say in praise of Camir Silmuna, but our land is indelibly marked by his legacy.”
Lucas síl Bellacaire, The History of the Lilac River, Vol. II

description.text:
“Do not fear death, my people. Fear nothing which you do in the company of brave souls; fear nothing which you do among your fellow citizens! We live in the time of the Mage-Emperors – in the era of the staff – and its power seems absolute. But we know these mages can die.

We knew it three hundred years ago, when the discipline of the fusillade first began to rival the arc of the fireball. We knew it two hundred years ago, when first we learned of that glorious substance, then accessible only so very far away, which could countermand their unearned gifts. And we know it now – now that their ritual of growth, their promise of endless harvest, has wrought a desolate steppe where once there was only verdant life. It is what they do! Addle the land, poison the water, wreck the bountiful Halann we share for the slightest chance at a lonely throne.

Hear me! It’s true – we may die today. But we die together, while they die alone.”
Carric of Paredocks, Final Address

player_overview.avoid_if: Players seeking highly mobile conquest from the opening or unwilling to maintain diplomacy.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Hold the Free City through defenses and relations, then unite the valley through Sway, allies, and measured wars.
player_overview.overview: You start as Bellacaire, an East Damerian fortress Free City. Walls, religious diplomats, and neutrality define it: stabilize neighbors and build defenses, then turn urban relief into a political resource. You still follow the shared Luna Sway, alliance, and Pashainé formation route.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy fortress defense, diplomatic neutrality, and protecting urban residents.
signature_features: Two exclusive missions revolve around religious diplomats, relations, walls, and urban relief.
The ideas recall the fortress struggle, Lilac War defense, and neutrality pacts.
20 shared Luna missions connect the fortress story to a city-state alliance.
player_overview.tagline: Turn a neutral fortress into a Free City that can withstand great armies and shelter refugees.

reasons: The clearest fortress-and-neutrality theme among the four cities
Religious diplomats and urban relief connect defense with a humanitarian story
warnings: The Pink Stripe upgrade is mission development, not an accomplished 1444 starting result

values.rationale: Neutrality, welcoming refugees, urban relief, and defense together form a strongly protective route; the regional alliance mainly serves autonomy and shelter, making this the most protective of the four Free Cities.
